Use case: compositing.
Asset type: finished agency portfolio project cover for Linc, a cloud production studio platform.
Primary request: Create a polished 1536 x 1024 pixel landscape image, exactly 3:2, composing the two supplied real Linc desktop product screenshots into one elegant layered presentation.
Input images: Image 1 (linc-2@2x.jpg) is the primary screen to preserve faithfully, showing the mountain lake asset manager. Image 2 (linc-3@2x.jpg) is the secondary screen to preserve faithfully, showing the production queue. Image 3 (Turtle screenshot) is ONLY a reference for the clean layered-screen presentation, soft blue atmospheric background, and sense of depth; do not copy its car UI, phones, text labels, cursor or application overlay.
Scene/backdrop: edge-to-edge refined cool cobalt blue and lavender ambient gradient, brighter periwinkle glow toward upper left, deep blue toward lower right; smooth, no decoration, no grain.
Composition: Two horizontal desktop product screens, front facing, no tilted perspective. Large primary mountain lake screen positioned upper right, approximately 75% of canvas width, with generous top/right breathing room. Smaller queue screen positioned lower left in foreground, approximately 58% of canvas width, overlapping only the bottom-left part of primary screen; retain the primary mountain photograph and right-hand version history clearly visible. Keep both screen aspect ratios intact and all outer screen boundaries inside the canvas. Avoid the look of a flat screenshot placed in the center; make the layered composition visually deliberate.
Styling: subtle rounded screen corners, very slim neutral edge, soft realistic diffuse shadows beneath each floating screen, premium minimal digital product presentation. Crop away the original screenshots' surrounding white matte. Preserve their existing thin desktop window bars, purple navigation, gray sidebar, exact icon styles, mountain imagery, table columns, and original UI layout. Scale supplied screen pixels faithfully, do not redesign or add content to the user interfaces.
Text: only text already contained within the two real supplied screens, faithfully retained. No separate headline, project name, marketing copy, caption, annotation, cursor circle, "VIEW PROJECT", watermark, browser interface outside the screens, or Codex interface.
Constraints: The supplied screens are real portfolio work. Preserve their UI design and proportions as carefully as possible; no invented mobile versions, no phones, no laptop hardware, no fabricated charts, no extra floating panels. Deliver the image alone.
